extracted.intended_audience: state permitting authorities and SIP submitters (e.g., PADEP), regulated electric generating unit owners/operators, environmental attorneys, EPA reviewers, and public stakeholders submitting comments
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating state SIP revisions that establish Reasonably Available Control Technology (RACT) emission limits for large electric generating units (EGUs), focusing on enforceability, technical/economic justification, alternative emission limits, and data support. Produces criteria used by EPA to decide whether to approve or disapprove SIP revisions under the Clean Air Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, objective applicability and enforceability of SCR-on lb/MMBtu limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits and SIP submissions must set forth clear, objective criteria for determining when emissions from each EGU are subject to the SCR-on lb/MMBtu daily average limit(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicability criteria are not clear and objective, EPA or the public cannot determine when the limit applies or whether the source is in noncompliance; lack of such criteria renders the limit effectively unenforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on director's discretion to alter SIP requirements or grant post-hoc exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: SIP provisions cannot contain director's discretion to alter SIP requirements, including variances or outright exemptions for emissions during startup/shutdown/malfunction or other periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-hoc determinations allowing the director to decide whether emissions are counted toward a more stringent limit constitute the type of unilateral, ad hoc decision EPA has barred (see 2015 SSM SIP Action and 1999 SSM guidance). Such provisions negate enforceability and are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined bounds and procedures for exclusions (startup, shutdown, emergency, technical infeasibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusions for events (e.g., 'start-up, and shut-down; operation pursuant to emergency generation required by PJM; periods in which compliance would require operation inconsistent with technological limitations, good engineering and maintenance practices, and/or good air pollution control practices') must be defined in the permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits must identify what constitutes each excluded condition, the general factors that may lead to a determination (e.g., technical infeasibility), whom the permittee demonstrates infeasibility to, and how EPA/public can review and verify such demonstrations; vague or unbounded exclusion language is difficult or impossible to enforce.

rubrics_metrics.name: No sole permittee discretion in determining applicability in periodic reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits should not allow sources to have sole discretion to indicate in monthly reports 'whether or not they believe they are subject to the [SCR-on] lb NOx/MMBtu limit' or to 'clearly document how [they] determined' applicability without objective verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing the source to self-determine applicability without objective criteria prevents EPA and the public from independently assessing compliance; reporting frameworks must enable third-party verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Emission Limits (AELs) must be explicit, meet RACT, and be enforceable
rubrics_metrics.description: Any alternative emission limitations (different limits for different modes of operation) 'must be clearly stated components of the emission limitation, must meet the applicable level of control required for the type of SIP provision (e.g., be RACT for sources located in nonattainment areas) and must be legally and practicably enforceable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must explain how the combination of AELs satisfies CAA requirements; EPA will evaluate whether the AELs function together to meet RACT and enforcement expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of EPA-recommended criteria when developing AELs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA recommended seven criteria (2015 SSM SIP Action) that states should consider when developing alternative emission limits to assure they meet basic CAA requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIP submissions relying on AELs should demonstrate how they satisfy those recommended criteria; failure to address them undermines EPA approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: RACT limits must represent the lowest achievable rates considering technological and economic feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected RACT limits (SCR-on daily average lb/MMBtu, all-conditions daily lb/MMBtu, and 30-day rolling lb/hr) must be justified as the lowest rates that can be achieved considering technological and economic feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State must demonstrate with data/analysis that the chosen limits reflect achievable minimums (periods of good control) rather than business-as-usual averages or higher-emitting periods; general claims of 'optimization' without supporting data are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification and quantification for upward adjustments and compliance margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Any upward adjustment to limits (e.g., to account for lag time, changes in operating patterns, aging equipment) or application of a 'compliance margin' buffer must be explained and quantified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must explain what the margin is, why it is necessary to make the limit technically/economically feasible, how fluctuations/load/lag/future operations affect the lowest achievable rate, and provide the numeric margin applied; unexplained percentage buffers (e.g., 10–21%) are not adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete, appropriate data/timeframe selection and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset and timeframes used to select limits must be appropriate and justified (e.g., PADEP relied on 2017–2020 data but did not show why earlier years were excluded or why the chosen years represent the lowest achievable rates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses should include sufficient data across representative periods and explain why selected years reflect current capabilities (including effects of equipment aging or modifications). A limited qualitative description of selected months/years without full supporting data is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day rolling average lb/hr limit must constrain operation without SCRs and prevent circumvention
rubrics_metrics.description: The all-conditions 30-day rolling average lb/hr limit is intended to 'hold the three emission limits together' by limiting how much the source can operate without SCRs over extended periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State must demonstrate that the 30-day lb/hr rate forces operators to maximize SCR operation and prevents gaming (e.g., prolonged low-load operations that meet lb/MMBtu but avoid SCR use) similar to the '600-degree temperature' loophole; if the 30-day limit does not accomplish this, it does not meet RACT.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day rolling average lb/hr limit must be derived from full analysis, not selective snapshots
rubrics_metrics.description: When using 30-day rolling averages to justify lb/hr limits, the state must present complete analysis over the full timeframe evaluated (e.g., 2017–2020) rather than graphs restricted to a single season or year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must be able to determine whether the selected lb/hr limit represents an average of multiple years (problematic) or the lowest lb/hr achieved when considering techno-economic feasibility; selective presentation impedes verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIP revisions cannot preauthorize unilateral state changes to SIP emission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA cannot approve SIP provisions that 'automatically preauthorize the state to unilaterally revise the SIP emission limit (in this case by making determinations that it did not apply at certain times)' without following SIP revision procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any process that would allow the state to change when a limit applies or to exempt emissions without EPA approval violates procedural and substantive SIP revision requirements under the CAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion language tied to 'technological limitations, good engineering/maintenance practices, and/or good air pollution control practices' must be operationalized
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases excluding periods 'in which compliance with this emission limit would require operation of any equipment in a manner inconsistent with technological limitations, good engineering and maintenance practices, and/or good air pollution control practices' require further definition and instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits must provide interpretation/application guidance so the exemption is not open-ended; otherwise the exemption undermines enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and monitoring must enable independent public/EPA oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordkeeping and reporting requirements must be structured so EPA and the public can determine which hours of emissions count toward limits and whether the source complied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reports leave critical determinations to the permittee or lack objective criteria, third-party oversight and enforcement are impossible; EPA cites Sierra Club v. EPA regarding the necessity of adequate recordkeeping to enable oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 110(l) non-interference demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Under CAA section 110(l), EPA cannot approve a SIP revision 'if the revision would interfere with any applicable requirement concerning attainment and reasonable further progress ... or any other applicable requirement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must demonstrate that approval will not increase emissions or otherwise interfere with attainment; EPA's analysis of interference is case-specific and requires sufficient information to conclude no interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot rely on non–EPA-approved out-of-state regulations as justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Citing a neighboring state's regulation (e.g., Maryland COMAR 26.11.38.04) as support is ineffective unless EPA has approved that regulation as RACT for EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should identify only SIP-approved RACT regulations if relying on comparators; otherwise the comparison carries no weight in EPA's approval analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of SCR-on setpoints must be justified with unit-specific evidence and explain applicability of cross-unit studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where studies show effects (e.g., catalyst fouling, pressure drop) at certain SCR setpoints, states must explain how those findings apply to each unit and why selected setpoints avoid those problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applying another facility's study to a different unit requires explanation of comparability; unit-specific conditions (e.g., economizer bypass, SCR upgrades) must be considered and the rationale for chosen setpoints documented.
